title: Operational-Condition-Aware Reliability Assessment of MQTT-Based Wireless Sensing in Smart Greenhouses
content: Recently, high-frequency wireless sensing technologies have been widely adopted in smart greenhouse environments for real-time environmental monitoring and automated control. However, long-term sensor data reliability can degrade due to wireless communication instability, power fluctuation, and environmental variations under high-frequency sensing conditions. Existing studies have mainly focused on anomaly detection and abnormal data filtering, while reliability degradation under real operational conditions has received limited attention. In this study, abnormal sensor data fluctuation phenomena occurring in high-frequency wireless smart greenhouse environments were defined as Reliability Collapse. The proposed Reliability Collapse was classified into Spike Collapse, Oscillation Collapse, Drift Collapse, and Dropout Collapse. In addition, Collapse Frequency (CF), Reliability Index (RI), and Collapse Severity Score (CSS) were defined to quantitatively evaluate sensing reliability degradation. Experiments were conducted for approximately one month using MQTT-based ESP32 wireless sensor nodes under different operational conditions, including sampling interval variations, RSSI conditions, power stability, and high-humidity/condensation environments. Experimental results showed that shorter sampling intervals, degraded RSSI conditions, unstable power supply, and high-humidity environments significantly increased Reliability Collapse occurrence and reduced long-term sensing reliability. In particular, the 0.5 s sensing condition increased Spike Collapse and Oscillation Collapse occurrence, while weak RSSI conditions increased Dropout Collapse frequency. The results demonstrate that multiple operational conditions, including sampling interval, wireless communication quality, power stability, and environmental conditions, are associated with degradation in long-term sensing reliability.
